The H1 2026 weighted average (210.3m) understates the period-end reduction; the point-in-time count is used.

The current portion of lease obligations sits inside 'Other' current liabilities and is not separately disclosed (under JPY1bn; ignored).

inputs.buyback_note: JPY15,002m purchase of treasury shares in H1 2026 (financing cash flow). FY2019-FY2025 repurchases were JPY0-3m/yr. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (flat count); the May-2026 buyback is reflected in the share count, and the cash is reflected in the 30-Jun-2026 net debt. Management has said cross-shareholding sale proceeds (~70% reduction by end-2028) will fund further buybacks.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close, Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. Rf 1.6% (10y JGB, Oct-2026), ERP 6.0%, beta 1.3 (commodity carbon black / graphite electrode cyclical with semiconductor-capex exposure) -> cost of equity ~9.4%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.5% (bonds, CP and bank loans; JCR A+ / R&I A); market-value weights ~75/25 -> ~7.4%, rounded UP to 8.0% to sit nearer the ~9% house reference for JPY industrials. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: A (leases as debt). J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating income already; the JPY8,874m 'Lease obligations' line is finance leases (leased assets, net JPY9,006m), so it is added to net debt once and NOT deducted from the flows. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (segment EBITDA includes majority-owned subsidiaries, e.g. Tokai COBEX, the Thai carbon black JV). NCI of JPY34,733m at 30-Jun-2026 is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book (NCI profit share was JPY3.2bn in FY2025, so book ~11x is a fair proxy). Calibration: FY2026E EBIT 35.0bn x (1-31%) = 24.2bn vs guided net income 22.0bn + NCI ~3bn - ~10bn extraordinary gain on securities sales + ~1bn net non-operating = ~16bn attributable operating-only; the gap is the extraordinary gain and non-operating dividend/FX income, both outside the flows and inside the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Tokai Carbon is a diversified industrial carbon materials maker (carbon black 46%, smelting & lining 19%, fine carbon/SiC 17%, graphite electrodes 12%, furnaces 3%); not a financial, REIT or holdco. FY2024 is NOT a usable base: the JPY56.5bn net loss carried a JPY68.1bn impairment and JPY8.0bn restructuring charge below operating income, so the build anchors to FY2025 actuals (revenue 322,960, EBITDA 58,442 = 18.1%) and FY2026 guidance (revised twice, Aug-2026: sales 386,000, OI 35,000, EBITDA 72,400 = 18.8%, capex ~43.1bn, D&A incl. goodwill ~37.4bn) rather than to any single year's FCF, then glides to a mid-cycle EBITDA margin. EBITDA margin history (company definition, OI + D&A incl. goodwill amortisation): FY2019 29.4% (electrode super-cycle), FY2020 17.5%, FY2021 21.1%, FY2022 22.2%, FY2023 20.9%, FY2024 17.5%, FY2025 18.1%, FY2026E 18.8%; mid-cycle ex-2019 is ~19.5%, Vision 2030 targets 20%. Base year choice: FY0 = FY2025, Y1 = FY2026 at guidance, discounted one full period, with the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet and the post-buyback share count -- this double-counts H1 2026 FCF (JPY4.6bn, ~JPY23/share) but over-discounts FY2026 by ten months, net slightly conservative. Interest income (JPY1,845m FY2025) is non-operating and is excluded from the EBITDA-based flows; cash is netted in the bridge, so it is stripped from last_fcf too. Dividend income on cross-shareholdings is likewise non-operating and outside the flows; the matching asset (investment securities) is in the equity_bridge after tax. Capex has run above D&A for a decade (12-14% vs 10% of revenue, Thai plant and relocation projects), which is why reported FCF averaged only ~JPY12bn on ~JPY300bn revenue in FY2019-25; the base case lets capex fall to 9.5% of revenue as the Thai build (CIP JPY32.5bn) completes, i.e. an FCF conversion MORE generous than history, and the valuation still sits well below the market price. The market is paying ~7x FY2026E EV/EBITDA and ~18x the guided (gain-inflated) net income for the SiC focus-ring / AI-capex story; this model does not grant that re-rating in the base case.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (cross-shareholdings) at 30-Jun-2026 fair value, after tax

Management plans to sell ~70% by end-2028 (May-2026 capital policy), so realisation is credible; dividend income on these is outside the operating flows, satisfying the matching-asset rule.
H1 2026 balance sheet. Flows are consolidated; NCI charged once, here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal growth after the FY2026 guidance step-up; equity CAGRs are inflated by FX translation (foreign currency translation adjustment JPY112bn in AOCI) and the 5yr EPS CAGR is off a trough FY2020 base (EPS JPY4.78)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.6% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 81.5% (trough-base artefact) and revenue 3yr CAGR -1.7% vs equity 3yr 5.8%: divergence >30% on both; FY2024 impairment and FX translation dominate the equity series, so equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Bases: revenue FY2020 201,542 -> FY2025 322,960; FY2022 340,371 -> FY2025. EPS FY2020 4.78 / FY2022 105.16 -> FY2025 94.05. Equity FY2020 201,267 / FY2022 268,827 -> FY2025 318,358. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 27,578 -> FY2025 11,020; FY2022 owner FCF was -4,613 (capex 45.2bn), so the 3yr CAGR is undefined. Owner-FCF CAGR (-16.8%) is below reported (-14.1%) only because interest income has risen with rates, not because of SBC (nil). The message of the FCF series is that capex has absorbed EBITDA growth: FY2019-FY2025 owner FCF averaged ~JPY10bn (~3.5% of revenue) against EBITDA of ~JPY63bn.

base.narrative: Y1 = FY2026 at the Aug-2026 revised guidance (sales 386.0bn, EBITDA 72.4bn / 18.8%, capex 43.1bn = 11.2%, D&A 37.4bn = 9.7%). Thereafter revenue grows at 2-4% nominal (Vision 2030's 500bn is reached ~2035, not 2030), EBITDA margin drifts to a 19.5% mid-cycle plateau (below the 20% Vision 2030 target), capex normalises to 9.5% of revenue as the Thai plant and relocation projects complete, roughly matching D&A. Cash tax 31% (Japan statutory ~30.6%; FY2025 cash tax 9.3bn on 26bn pre-tax). Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory of ~172bn vs payables of ~25bn, so growth consumes cash at 15% of the revenue change (below the ~45% NWC intensity, reflecting management's inventory and receivables discipline). Terminal: 1.5% growth, cap 15x FCF (implies ~5x terminal EV/EBITDA, inside the stock's 5-8x history).

bull.narrative: Vision 2030 delivered: revenue ~490bn by FY2030 (6-7% CAGR after the FY2026 step-up) as solid-SiC focus rings ride the memory/AI capex cycle, MLCC-linked furnace demand compounds, Middle East smelter restarts and RuC licensing lift Smelting & Lining, and US AD/CVD duties on Indian/Chinese electrodes hold, letting Graphite Electrodes earn a sustained mid-single-digit margin. Mix shift to Fine Carbon takes group EBITDA margin to 21% by FY2030 (above the 20% target). Capex discipline post-Thai plant (9% of revenue) converts the margin into FCF. Terminal growth 2.0% with the 15x cap.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands a little under guidance (H2 carbon black pass-through slips), then a FY2027-28 downturn: tire-OEM production cuts and Chinese carbon black exports pull Carbon Black volumes down, the US electrode duties are weakened or Chinese/Indian supply reroutes, the memory capex cycle rolls over and SiC power-semi demand stays sluggish. Revenue falls 11% over two years, EBITDA margin troughs at 15% (FY2020-24 trough band was 17.5% at the group level, with segments individually loss-making), and recovers only to 17%. Capex stays above D&A (10.5% vs 10%) because the relocation and environmental projects cannot be deferred. Terminal growth 0.5%, 12x cap -- the commodity-cyclical multiple. No goodwill impairment is modelled explicitly (non-cash), but the JPY24.7bn goodwill and JPY20.3bn customer-related intangibles remaining would be at risk on this path.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance year as revised in August 2026 (sales +19.5%, EBITDA 18.8%), then a mature cyclical: 2-4% nominal growth, 19.5% mid-cycle EBITDA margin, capex falling to match D&A at 9.5% of revenue. The axes are (1) carbon black volume/price pass-through against tire-OEM cycles and Chinese export pressure, (2) SiC focus-ring volumes against the memory capex cycle, (3) whether the graphite-electrode profit holds once the US duty tailwind is tested, and (4) capex discipline after the Thai build. Base assumes the business earns its Vision 2030 margin only partially and never converts more than ~6-7% of revenue into owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vision 2030 largely achieved -- ~490bn revenue by FY2030 and 21% EBITDA margin on Fine Carbon mix, with capex normalising to 9% of revenue and electrode duties intact; the capital-return programme (40% payout, 5% DOE floor, cross-shareholding sales funding buybacks) is executed as announced.
scenario_narratives.bear: A FY2027-28 industrial downturn on the three commodity legs (tires, EAF steel, aluminium) coinciding with a memory capex rollover; margin troughs at 15%, capex cannot be cut below D&A, and the electrode turnaround proves policy-contingent. The company stays solvent (net D/E 0.38x, A ratings) but the equity is a low-return cyclical.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because three of the five segments are commodity cyclicals that have each been loss-making within the last three years, the electrode recovery leans on a trade remedy, and the FY2024 impairment shows how fast acquired goodwill can evaporate. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things -- the memory cycle, electrode duties, Middle East smelter demand and post-Thai capex discipline -- to hold simultaneously through 2030. No going-concern risk (net D/E 0.38x, JCR A+), so bear is not weighted higher than that.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a mid-cycle margin and a normalised capex ratio, because neither FY2024 (impairment-distorted) nor FY2025 (recovery year, 13bn FCF) is a repeatable base. The build is deliberately more generous on FCF conversion than the company's own decade (capex at 9.5% of revenue vs 12-14% actual) and still values the equity well below the market price: the share price embeds a re-rating on the SiC / AI-capex narrative and the capital-return programme that the base case does not grant. The cross-shareholding portfolio (JPY42bn after tax) and NCI (JPY35bn) are bridged explicitly; dividend and interest income are excluded from the flows to match.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity: every 1pp of revenue in perpetual capex is worth roughly JPY60/share; the base case assumes capex falls to D&A, which the company has not achieved since FY2019.
Cyclical trough timing: a tire/steel/aluminium downturn in the explicit window (bear) takes the weighted value down sharply; the stock has rerated 2.2x in twelve months on the up-cycle.
Graphite electrode profit depends partly on US AD/CVD duties effective mid-2026 -- policy-contingent.
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 8%/1.5% (~15.6x FCF) sits just above the 15x cap; a 1pp WACC change moves the base value materially (see sensitivity).
Investment securities are bridged at after-tax fair value; a market fall before the planned 2026-28 disposals reduces this JPY200/share of value.
FX: ~60% of revenue is non-JPY; yen strength lowers reported EBITDA (FY2026 guidance assumes USD/JPY 159).
